purpose: Bounded DOL PAID program route showing employer self-audit, WHD review, prompt payment, and proof-of-payment requirements without treating employer documentation as worker-level recovery.

events.geography: United States; U.S. Department of Labor Wage and Hour Division PAID program
events.date_precision: current official PAID program description checked 2026-09-19; program rules and availability can change
events.denominator: Employers and affected employees considered for PAID; no public episode denominator or worker-level follow-up panel
events.method: Structured extraction from the official DOL PAID program and questions-and-answers pages
events.missingness: Named employer episode, affected worker identities, amounts, payment instruments, worker receipt/cashing, adequacy, remaining loss, household effect, later work, trust, recurrence, and exit are not retained
events.exposure: Employer self-audit identifies potential minimum-wage, overtime, or qualifying FMLA violations affecting employees
events.alternatives_before_action: Private claim, union, legal aid, litigation, continued work, other employment, and non-use alternatives are not observed for any affected worker
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: The program creates a formal route for calculating back wages or other remedies and requires prompt employer payment after WHD review; worker-level adequacy and timing remain unknown
events.choice_or_response: Employer audits and reports potential violations; WHD reviews the scope and calculations; employer pays within 15 days of the summary and provides proof of payment; an employee may accept or decline the offered payment
events.person_or_actor_with_control: Employer controls self-audit, calculation, payment, and practice correction; WHD controls review and program acceptance; workers control whether to accept or decline, but their practical options are not observed
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: PAID supplies a voluntary employer-correction route, WHD review, employee-specific settlement forms, a 15-day payment requirement, proof-of-payment documentation, and prospective correction of the pay or leave practice
events.remedy_receipt: Employer proof of payment is required, but the public program description does not establish a named worker's delivery, cashing, acceptance, or adequate use of the money
events.durability_followup: The route requires correction of the identified practice but provides no public same-worker or later-payroll outcome showing durable compliance, recurrence, household recovery, trust, or exit
events.immediate_outcome: A stronger institutional payment-verification checkpoint exists between remedy calculation and worker-level recovery
events.protected_outcome: The design can protect against an order-only remedy by requiring employer evidence of payment and documentation of other remedies
events.sacrificed_outcome: Workers may still bear uncertainty about delivery, adequacy, remaining loss, or future workplace conditions; worker effort and alternative costs are not measured
events.cost_risk_transfer: The route shifts calculation and payment responsibility to the employer while leaving worker receipt, cashing, and later security outside the public record
events.later_outcome: The program ends publicly at employer payment proof and practice-correction documentation, not at worker-confirmed recovery or durable security
events.meaning_and_attribution: The program frames correction as voluntary compliance and employee choice; worker legitimacy, dignity, trust, and attribution are not measured
events.public_or_collective_response: The public route supplies an institutional correction channel; no worker-level complaint, organizing, political response, or exit is observed
events.counterexample: Proof that an employer paid WHD does not prove that a worker received, cashed, or found the payment sufficient, and an employee may decline payment without the public record showing why
events.source_and_uncertainty: Official U.S. Department of Labor Wage and Hour Division PAID and PAID Q&A pages, checked 2026-09-19; program architecture is public, but no named episode or worker outcome is retained

events.geography: United States; U.S. Department of Labor Wage and Hour Division PAID program
events.date_precision: official DOL program performance release covering launch through September 15, 2019
events.denominator: 7,429 employees in PAID actions concluded by the reported period; aggregate program denominator, not a worker follow-up panel
events.method: Structured extraction from the official DOL WHD PAID performance release
events.missingness: Individual employee identity, employer, amount, payment instrument, delivery/cashing, adequacy, remaining loss, household effect, later work, trust, recurrence, and exit are not retained
events.exposure: PAID self-audits identified potential minimum-wage and overtime violations and calculated back wages for affected employees
events.alternatives_before_action: Individual litigation, private settlement, union/legal-aid route, continued work, other employment, and non-use alternatives are not observed
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: DOL reported more than $4 million in back wages put into the hands of 7,429 employees through PAID by the covered date
events.choice_or_response: Employers self-audited and worked with WHD; the program reported prompt payment and compliance correction, but no employee-level response is retained
events.person_or_actor_with_control: Employers and WHD controlled the self-audit, review, calculation, payment, and compliance route; individual worker control is not observed in the aggregate release
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: The PAID program delivered an aggregate reported wage-remedy result and was described as improving speed and resource efficiency relative to traditional investigations
events.remedy_receipt: The release uses aggregate language that wages were put into employees' hands; it does not identify each employee's receipt, cashing, amount, or adequacy
events.durability_followup: No same-worker or employer-level later payroll, recurrence, household, trust, continued-work, or exit follow-up is supplied
events.immediate_outcome: Aggregate reported wage delivery is visible for 7,429 employees, stronger than a program rule alone
events.protected_outcome: The reported aggregate result indicates that a payment route reached employees in the program population, but the protected outcome for each worker is unknown
events.sacrificed_outcome: The release does not show residual wage loss, time spent, household trade-offs, or workers who did not receive or use the reported payments
events.cost_risk_transfer: The route reduces litigation and agency resource costs in aggregate while leaving individual adequacy, receipt, and later security unmeasured
events.later_outcome: The public endpoint stops at aggregate reported delivery and efficiency comparisons, not worker-level recovery or durability
events.meaning_and_attribution: The agency frames PAID as efficient correction; employee fairness, trust, dignity, and attribution are not measured
events.public_or_collective_response: Aggregate program performance is reported; no worker-level complaint, organizing, political response, or exit is observed
events.counterexample: A large aggregate amount put into employees' hands can coexist with unknown individual receipt, adequacy, residual loss, and later security
events.source_and_uncertainty: Official DOL WHD PAID performance release checked 2026-09-19; aggregate program result with no employee-level identifiers or follow-up

arrows.evidence: DOL describes identification of affected employees, calculation of back wages, reporting to WHD, and WHD review
arrows.counterexample: A program description does not establish that a particular employer completed an accurate audit
arrows.remaining_gap: Named employer episode, worker roster, calculation, scope, and review result

arrows.evidence: DOL requires employers to pay back wages or remedies within 15 days of receiving the summary
arrows.counterexample: A deadline is a program rule, not evidence of compliance in a named episode
arrows.remaining_gap: Payment date, amount, instrument, and employer-specific compliance

arrows.to: proof of payment and remedy documentation to WHD
arrows.evidence: DOL requires proof of payment and documentation of other remedies to be provided to WHD expeditiously
arrows.counterexample: Proof supplied to an agency is not the same as worker cashing or adequate use
arrows.remaining_gap: Named proof record, worker receipt, cashing, fees, and remaining loss

arrows.evidence: PAID requires records showing that the employer corrected the compensation or leave practices at issue
arrows.counterexample: Practice-correction documentation does not establish later payroll accuracy or absence of recurrence
arrows.remaining_gap: Post-correction payroll, recurrence, worker voice, and durable compliance

arrows.to: worker usable recovery and later security
arrows.evidence: The public PAID route describes proof and employee acceptance/decline but supplies no same-worker later outcome
arrows.counterexample: Payment proof can coexist with non-cashing, insufficient compensation, unresolved household loss, continued dependence, or exit
arrows.remaining_gap: Worker receipt/cashing, adequacy, residual loss, household outcome, continued work, trust, recurrence, and exit

arrows.evidence: DOL reported more than $4 million in back wages put into the hands of 7,429 employees through PAID by September 15, 2019
arrows.counterexample: The aggregate release does not identify which employee received what amount or when
arrows.remaining_gap: Employer and worker episode identifiers, amount, payment date, and payment rail

arrows.evidence: The release reports 7,429 employees in the PAID performance result
arrows.counterexample: A program denominator is not a complete or independently verified recipient denominator
arrows.remaining_gap: Eligible, paid, returned, uncashed, and successfully received employee counts

arrows.evidence: DOL reports that PAID actions took less time and yielded more back wages per staff hour than comparison traditional investigations, while employers corrected practices
arrows.counterexample: Aggregate efficiency does not establish durable payroll accuracy at any named employer
arrows.remaining_gap: Employer-level correction, later payroll, recurrence, and worker voice

arrows.evidence: The release reports aggregate delivery but supplies no employee-level later outcome
arrows.counterexample: Aggregate payment delivery can coexist with insufficient amount, non-cashing, residual loss, or continued household insecurity
arrows.remaining_gap: Same-worker receipt, adequacy, household effect, continued work, trust, recurrence, and exit

arrows.evidence: No later worker or household outcome is reported in the performance release
arrows.counterexample: A one-time wage payment does not establish durable job security, restored household room, trust, or a chosen exit
arrows.remaining_gap: Later employment, recurrence, household security, trust, switching, and exit

boundary: This ledger closes a public institutional payment-verification architecture, not a worker-level payment, recovery, adequacy, or durable-security outcome. It must not be pooled with named case receipts or treated as a recovery rate.
storage_boundary: No employer self-audit, payroll, worker identity, payment, bank, or restricted file is retained; only the official public program route and explicit unresolved stages are represented.
